subject: general
question: Positive skewness means that the frequencies in the distribution are spread:

options.text: on the left side of the centre of the curve
uniformly on both sides of the centre of the curve
on the right side of the centre of the curve
on neither side of the centre of the curve

solution:
The correct answer is** on the right side of the centre of the curve.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Positive skewness means that the frequencies in the distribution are spread on the right side of the centre of the curve:**

 
 
• In a positively skewed distribution, most of the data points (frequencies) are concentrated on the left side, with a long tail extending to the right. This indicates that there are a few unusually high values pulling the mean to the right.
 
• In the context of financial enterprises, positive skewness can suggest that while most investment returns are below average, there are some significant outliers with very high returns. This can be crucial for risk assessment and portfolio management.
 
• Understanding the skewness helps in making more informed decisions regarding risk and return trade-offs. For example, positively skewed assets might be more attractive to risk-seeking investors due to the potential for high returns.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **on the left side of the centre of the curve:**

 
 
• This is incorrect because data concentrated on the left side would indicate negative skewness, not positive skewness.
 
• In negatively skewed distributions, the tail extends to the left, suggesting most data points are higher with a few low outliers.
 
 
 
• **uniformly on both sides of the centre of the curve:**
 
 
• This describes a symmetrical distribution, not a skewed one. A symmetrical distribution implies that data points are evenly spread on both sides of the mean, resulting in no skewness.
 
• Symmetrical distributions are often associated with normal distributions, which are crucial for many statistical analyses.
 
 
 
• **on neither side of the centre of the curve:**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because it does not describe any known type of skewness or distribution pattern.
 
• For a distribution to be skewed, the data must be asymmetrically distributed either to the left or right of the centre.
